newsitem.title: USA: SMITHFIELD FOODS FINED $12.6 MLN -- US EPA.
newsitem.headline: SMITHFIELD FOODS FINED $12.6 MLN -- US EPA.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said Friday a U.S. District Court fined Smithfield Foods Inc and two of its subsidiaries $12.6 million for discharging illegal levels of pollutants.
The agency said Smithfield was fined for discharging the pollutants from their slaughterhouse operations into the Pagan River, in violation of the federal Clean Water Act.
It said Judge Rebecca Beech Smith of U.S. District Court in Norfolk, Va. imposed the largest fine ever for a water pollution case.
The agency said the subsidiaries, Smithfield Packing Co and Gwaltney of Smithfield Ltd, each operate a hog slaughtering and processing plant in Smithfield, Va. where the violations occurred.
On Friday, Smithfield said its discharges to the Pagan River ended Wednesday when its Smithfield Packing Co waste water system was connected to the Hampton Roads Sanitation District's pipeline.
